blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff (§12.3); mixed-fat-object compatibility
blocking.problem: This changes certificate layout but supplies no mixed-fat-object integration statement. Neither the diff nor INDEX specifies that context inventories are scoped to device roots rather than the native host binary. This fails the explicit standing C7 check, which requires that statement for certificate-layout changes. Preserving nested region calls alone does not discharge it.
blocking.fix: Append to §12.3: 'For a mixed fat object, these frame records describe only the linked ISA regions in a bound device-root realisation. Each scheduled device root has its own certificate bindings and context set; [] is relative to that root. The native host component invokes device code through §10, using a device CC entry where required. Native host functions need no frame records, and this inventory does not require unmarked host code to be lowered to ISA. Certificates for different roots may reference the same linked closure, but their frame contexts remain scoped to their respective root bindings.' Alternatively place this rule in a shared normative mixed-object clause and explicitly incorporate it here; prefer the local paragraph.

suggestions: Conformance vectors: publish a serialized pair/flip frame_contexts example. With H_pair denoting the pair closure hash, use keys [{symbol:H_pair,point:"entry:0",iteration:[],instance:[],call_index:0}] and [{symbol:H_pair,point:"entry:1",iteration:[],instance:[],call_index:0}], selecting mut:0/class A/width 1 and mut:0/class B/width 1 respectively. Include all five required B5 arrays. State: 'A default-covered call requires its record even when entries is empty; replacing the second class by A rejects.'

Release and route: record the requested compatibility decision explicitly: 'This is a council-authorized 0.9 K certificate repair with unchanged source/version envelopes. Existing uniform frame records retain their encoding and undergo all-context validation. Producers regenerate nonuniform certificates; consumers must not discard frame_contexts or substitute its first descriptor for the complete array.' This makes migration concrete without changing the ref@0.9 catalog.
path_to_accept: Add V2V-1's normative device-root/mixed-fat-object scoping paragraph. No other blocking change is required; retain the proposed frame selection, complete context coverage and uniform shorthand.
summary: The defect, cited premises, witness arithmetic and conditional hash claims check out. The context-indexed repair is sound. One contract blocker remains: explicitly preserve mixed-fat-object packaging and scope frame inventories to device roots.
